_notes: Configured June 2026. Standard BigCommerce theme (ul.productGrid, h1.page-heading). No SearchSpring — native BC sort/search. Native BC search always returns results (full catalog for any term) — no zero-result state. Quote-only catalog (no prices, no cart, no qty input, no lead-time). Mobile nav is #mySidenav. Mobile breadcrumbs hidden. Footer root is plain <footer> (no .tcsFooter). No .Contact-info-box — contact info in footer .box:last-child. No payment icons. PLP at /aluminum/. Sidebar is .sidebarBlock. No subcategory tiles. PDP: no qty steppers, no carousel, no Yotpo, no SS recently-viewed. KNOWN SITE DEFICIENCY (test intentionally failing): products have no SKU set in BigCommerce admin — seo.cy.js JSON-LD Product block test fails. BRH admin must add SKUs (model numbers) to products. KNOWN SITE DEFICIENCY (test intentionally failing, verified July 28 2026 via direct HTML fetch): 2 of 15 pdp.popular products carry no spec-sheet PDF — /4-0-x-4-0-ee-single-leaf-roof-hatch-galvanized-steel-cover-and-curb-milcor/ and /24-x-38-fixed-deck-mounted-skylight-laminated-glass-fakro/ (the other 13 each have 1 PDF), so pdp.cy.js 'spec sheet links open PDFs in a new tab' (requires >=1 .pdf per PDP) fails ~13% of runs when the random pick lands on one — same deficiency class as CAD. This only became visible once the theme-error wrap let pdp.cy.js run past before-all. BRH admin must upload the manufacturer spec sheets for those 2 products in BigCommerce admin. Do NOT pin/exclude them from pdp.popular — that would mask the gap (site-deficiency policy). LIGHTHOUSE (calibrated July 2 2026, live scores homepage a11y 85 / plp 86 / pdp 79): all clear the fleet-wide accessibility:60 floor (no per-store override). KNOWN DEFICIENCY: homepage performance scored 42 vs the 50 floor (heavy content, fixable, not theme-structural) -> homepage Lighthouse test intentionally left failing; BRH devs must reduce homepage weight. KNOWN THEME BUGS (verified July 27-28 2026): the theme has MULTIPLE first-party bugs in its jQuery document-ready callbacks that throw on BRH pages (they fire for real users too): (1) heading-iteration JS calls .trim() on an undefined value ('Cannot read properties of undefined (reading trim)'), and (2) a ready callback calls $(...) when $ is not a function ('$ is not a function'). jQuery processes .ready()/Deferred callbacks asynchronously via window.setTimeout, and a throw inside one propagates out of that timer as an uncaught error that — confirmed live over several runs — never reaches the uncaught:exception handler in any suppressible way (not by message, not by stack, not via a capture-phase error listener). So they are prevented at the source: e2e.js registers a Cypress.on('window:before:load') that wraps the BRH window's setTimeout and swallows any throw whose stack shows the jQuery+bestroofhatches.com ready channel (code.jquery.com frames AND a bestroofhatches.com theme-callback frame). This is scoped by stack to exactly that channel, so it covers trim, '$ is not a function', and any further ready-callback bug in this theme without masking unrelated errors — and it lets the PDP/discovery/images suites actually run their assertions instead of dying in before-all. Temporary; BRH devs must fix the theme's document-ready scripts, then remove the wrap. Note: these surfaced only because commit d05ca7a replaced the old blanket uncaught:exception () => false (which swallowed everything) with a scoped handler; BRH ran 'green' before only because the blanket handler hid them. Also: Klaviyo email-capture popup is loaded (store-functional) and its telemetry fetch fails under Cypress, throwing an unhandled 'Failed to fetch' rejection → suppressed as third-party noise via KNOWN_BUGGY_SCRIPTS messagePattern /Failed to fetch/ (matched by message not stack because a fetch-rejection TypeError has a frameless stack in Chrome) + DEFAULT_IGNORE 'klaviyo' for the console-spy line (checks.js). Also: 1.door-pay.com tax-exempt form widget (bc_tax_exempt_form_load.js) throws 'setting hostUrl' on every BRH page load and is now blocked via THIRD_PARTY_HOSTS (door-pay.com) — vendor script bug, not ours.
